prompt: You are helping a support agent draft a response. A customer says their team upgraded yesterday and now CSV exports finish but produce an empty file. They tried Chrome and Firefox, cleared cache, and confirmed that dashboard data is visible. The workspace has 42 seats and uses SSO. Ask for only the diagnostics needed to distinguish a permissions issue from an export-worker issue, acknowledge the disruption, and provide a temporary workaround. Keep the response under 180 words and do not invent a resolution time.

Classify and respond to this support ticket: After rotating our API token, webhook deliveries began returning 401 even though regular API requests with the new token succeed. The webhook destination and signing secret were not changed. Failed deliveries started at 09:14 UTC and affect two projects, while a third project is healthy. Produce a concise customer reply, a private troubleshooting checklist for the agent, and the three most useful timestamps or identifiers to request. Avoid exposing internal infrastructure details.

A billing administrator reports that five invited users appear as active seats even though none accepted their invitation. The invoice closes tomorrow. The administrator already revoked and resent invitations once. Draft a calm response that separates what is known from what still needs verification, asks for workspace and invoice identifiers without requesting personal data, and explains the safest temporary action. Include a short internal escalation note with severity and impact.

A customer on a staging workspace sees intermittent 504 errors when generating reports longer than six months. Shorter ranges work, retries sometimes succeed, and no other pages are affected. Write a support response that acknowledges the pattern, gives two low-risk checks they can perform, states what evidence engineering needs, and avoids claiming that the root cause is known. Then provide a one-sentence ticket summary suitable for an incident queue.
